newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open bourse at record highs.
newsitem.headline: German shares open bourse at record highs.

text.p: German equities open bourse trade at new highs, boosted by positive sentiment in advance of Monday's Deutsche Telekom flotation and underpinned by a record close on Wall Street overnight and the strength of the dollar.
In early trade the DAX index, which gauges trade in 30 German blue-chip stocks, stood at 2,795.05, up 18.04 points or 0.65 percent, just shy of the psychologically important 2,800-point level.
"2,800 points would be great -- another new high, yet again -- and it looks very likely that that could be the case. Just look at the DAX futures contract," said a Frankfurt trader.
The DAX future stood at 2,806.50 points, up 12 points, in early bourse trade, which traders said was an inspirational position for the contract.

"This is very good, coming just before the Telekom flotation on Monday. The market is favouring different sectors in turn -- chemicals, utilities, cars and now the banks. This is a very healthy bull market," the trader said.
The three biggest German banks were among the heaviest-traded stocks in Frankfurt in early bourse trade.
Commerzbank AG was up 13 pfennigs at 36.78 marks and over one and a half million Commerzbank shares changed hands in early floor trade.
At the same time, Dresdner Bank AG was up 68 pfennigs at 45.08 marks and Deutsche Bank AG was up 28 pfennigs at 72.48 marks.

Electronics group Siemens AG was among the losers early on, down 25 pfennigs at 73.65 marks. Dealers said the group was suffering after profit warnings in its passive components and electron tubes division on Thursday and the poor outlook for the German electronics sector.
